name: Irrigation
overview: Scripture uses the concept of irrigation both literally and figuratively to illustrate God's provision and guidance. In Deuteronomy 11:10, irrigation is depicted as a necessary labor to cultivate the land, contrasting the fertile Promised Land with Egypt. Figuratively, Proverbs 21:1 compares the king's heart to rivers of water, emphasizing God's sovereign control over human affairs. Ecclesiastes 2:6 and Isaiah 58:11 further develop this imagery, portraying God's sustaining care as the watering of a garden that never fails, symbolizing continual spiritual nourishment and restoration even in times of drought.
